brief: Florence Nightingale was born in 1820. Dissatisfied with her comfortable life, she felt called by God to devote her life to nursing. She gained what little training was then available. She offered her services to the British army on the outbreak of the Crimean War in 1854, and was sent to the military hospital at Scutari in Turkey. Her selfless devotion to her task won her the acclaim of her patients and recognition for social service by women. By the time she died in 1910, nursing had become a valued and honoured profession.
